metadata.notes: Surprise questions are historical/fun about machines and humans. Recovery questions use humor and are easier.

questions.question: What did Ada Lovelace predict in 1843 that machines could do beyond calculation?
options: Create music, art, and manipulate symbols
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace envisioned computers creating music and art, predicting artificial intelligence over 100 years before computers existed!

questions.question: Why was Grace Hopper's team's first computer bug literally a bug?
options: It was a metaphor for errors
An actual moth was found stuck in a relay causing malfunctions
They named software errors after insects
questions.explanation: In 1947, a real moth was found in Harvard's Mark II computer relay, creating the term 'debugging' we still use today!

questions.question: What was the Jacquard Loom's revolutionary contribution to computing?
options: It was the first electric computer
Used punched cards for programmable patterns - inspiring early computers
It had nothing to do with computing
questions.explanation: The 1804 Jacquard Loom used punched cards to 'program' weaving patterns, directly inspiring Charles Babbage and early computing!

questions.question: Why did the database administrator leave their spouse?
options: Because there were too many foreign keys in the relationship
questions.explanation: Classic DBA humor - foreign keys create relationships between tables, just like... well, you get it! 😄

questions.question: What did Alan Turing propose in 1950 to test machine intelligence?
options: The Turing Test - can a machine's conversation fool a human judge?
questions.explanation: The Turing Test asks: if a human can't distinguish machine from human in conversation, can we call the machine intelligent?

questions.question: Who wrote the first algorithm intended for a machine (before computers existed)?
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843, making her the world's first programmer!

questions.question: Why do programmers prefer dark mode?
questions.explanation: Software bugs are attracted to light, obviously! 🐛💡 (And yes, dark mode is actually easier on the eyes too.)

questions.question: What was ENIAC's original purpose when built in 1945?
options: Calculating artillery firing tables for the US Army
questions.explanation: ENIAC, one of the first general-purpose computers, was built to calculate ballistic trajectories during WWII!

questions.question: If it takes 8 hours for 8 servers to process 8 terabytes of data, how long for 16 servers to process 16 terabytes?
questions.explanation: Still 8 hours! Each server processes 1TB in 8 hours. Double the servers AND double the data = same time. Linear scaling!

questions.question: What did the term 'computer' originally refer to before electronic machines?
options: A human person who performed calculations
questions.explanation: Before the 1940s, 'computers' were people (often women) employed to perform mathematical calculations by hand!

questions.question: Oops! That was tricky. Let's try something easier: What's the most important first step when production goes down?
options: Check if you can restore service quickly
questions.explanation: Step 1: Breathe. Step 2: Restore service. Step 3: Then investigate. You've got this! 💪

questions.question: No worries, happens to the best of us! Quick one: What do logs, metrics, and traces help you do?
options: Understand what's happening in production systems
questions.explanation: These three give you observability - like x-ray vision into your production systems! See? You knew that! ✨

questions.question: Hey, that last one was tough! Here's a gimme: What's better - spending all your time fighting fires, or automating solutions?
options: Automating solutions so you can build cool stuff
questions.explanation: Exactly! Work smarter, not harder. That's what AI for production systems is all about! 🚀

questions.question: Shake it off! Easy question: What's the goal of observability?
options: Generate as many dashboards as possible
Understand system behavior from external outputs
Collect data you'll never look at
questions.explanation: Bingo! It's about understanding, not just collecting. Quality over quantity! You're on a roll! 📊

questions.question: Not your fault that one was sneaky! Simple one: Why do we have staging environments?
options: To waste money on extra servers
questions.explanation: Test in staging, deploy to production with confidence! You're absolutely right! 🎯

questions.question: Don't worry, even senior engineers miss these sometimes! What does MTTR measure?
questions.explanation: Mean Time To Resolve - how fast you fix things! (Though Mean Time To Resume Netflix has its place too 😄)

questions.question: Hey, at least you learned something! Easy one: What's an incident?
options: When your code works on the first try
An event that degrades or disrupts service
Free pizza in the break room
questions.explanation: An incident is an unplanned service disruption. Now you're cooking! 🔥 (The good kind of fire!)

questions.question: That was a curveball! Straightforward one: What does CI/CD stand for?
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration and Deployment! (Though Coffee Integration is equally important ☕)

questions.question: It happens! Let's get back on track: What's a microservice?
options: A very small waiter at a restaurant
A service that's easy to understand
A miniature version of a monolith
questions.explanation: Small, focused services that can be deployed independently! You got it! 🎉

questions.question: Tricky one back there! Confidence booster: What's the cloud?
questions.explanation: The cloud is just someone else's computer! But fancier. And you don't have to maintain it! ☁️

questions.question: Everyone misses one sometimes! Quick win: What's toil in engineering?
options: Manual, repetitive work that doesn't scale
questions.explanation: Toil is the repetitive manual work we should automate! Less toil = more innovation! 💡

questions.question: That's okay, we're learning! Easy one: What's an API?
options: A Programming Interface that lets software talk to software
questions.explanation: APIs let services talk to each other! Like a universal translator for software! 🔌

questions.question: Keep going, you're doing great! What's a container?
options: A packaged application with its dependencies
questions.explanation: Containers package apps with everything they need to run anywhere! Like a lunchbox for code! 📦

questions.question: Shake it off! Simple question: What's deployment?
options: When you finally ship code to production
questions.explanation: Deployment = shipping your code live! The moment of truth! And you nailed this answer! 🚢

questions.question: Not your fault that was worded weirdly! What's a rollback?
options: Reverting to a previous working version
questions.explanation: When things break, rollback to the last good version! Your safety net! 🛟

questions.question: You're still here, that's what matters! What's monitoring?
options: Tracking metrics to know when things break
questions.explanation: Monitoring watches your systems so you can sleep at night! (Eventually!) 😴

questions.question: Let's reset with an easy win! What's a dependency?
options: Code or service that another system needs to work
questions.explanation: Dependencies are what your code needs to run! Like coffee for engineers! ☕ (That's a dependency too!)

questions.question: You've got this! What's latency?
options: The time between when something is late
The delay between request and response
questions.explanation: Latency is delay - how long things take! Low latency = fast = happy users! ⚡

questions.question: Almost there! What's a bug?
options: A feature that works too well
An error or flaw in code
Something that only happens to other people
questions.explanation: Bugs are errors in code! And yes, the first one was literally an insect! 🐛 You knew that!

questions.question: Finish strong! What's uptime?
options: The percentage of time a service is available and working
questions.explanation: Uptime = service is working! We all want 99.9%+ uptime! You're back on track! 🎯
